comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation accepts cash and securities as collateral for derivative contracts based on counterparty credit risk, nets cash collateral received against derivative assets, and pledges collateral on its own derivative positions, with further details in Note 3.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose practices involving the netting of cash collateral in the context of derivatives. JPMorgan highlights the impact of this netting on interest rates in geographic analysis (specifically against derivative payables), whereas Bank of America describes the general policy of netting cash collateral received against derivative assets based on master netting agreements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value percentage calculation methodology excluding cash collateral
comparisons.peer_summary: Percentages in the fair value tables are calculated based on total assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, excluding cash collateral paid or received on derivatives, because the cash collateral amounts have not been allocated to Level 1, 2, and 3 subtotals.
comparisons.comparison: While JPMorgan includes the impact of netted cash collateral in its rate analysis, Citigroup explicitly excludes cash collateral paid or received on derivatives from the calculation of percentages in its fair value tables because the amounts have not been allocated to specific fair value subtotals. This highlights a difference in how each firm handles cash collateral data within their supplementary financial disclosures: JPM incorporates it into rate calculations, whereas Citigroup excludes it from specific fair value percentage computations.
